title: Ramps & Speed
strapline: Steeper, faster, further — cars, balls and marbles racing down ramps children build and change themselves.
intent: Children investigate forces and motion — steeper ramps make things go faster and further.
Children test, predict and adjust, changing one thing at a time to see what happens.
Children build and connect ramps, guttering and tubes, solving how to make a run that works.
Children compare and measure — which went furthest, which was fastest, how far did it roll.
Children develop the language of forces and motion — push, roll, fast, slow, steep, gentle.
implementation: Provide ramps, guttering, tubes and blocks, and a range of things to roll — cars, balls, marbles.
Let children set the height and angle themselves and discover the effect of steeper and gentler.
Prompt prediction before each go — 'which will go furthest?' — then test and compare.
Encourage changing one thing at a time: same car, steeper ramp; same ramp, heavier ball.
Mark where things stop with tape or chalk and compare the distances directly.
Feed in the forces vocabulary — push, roll, speed up, slow down, steep, gentle, further.
Set challenges: make it reach the wall, make it jump the gap, make the slowest run you can.
key_questions: Which ramp do you think will make the car go fastest?
What happened when you made the ramp steeper?
Which one rolled the furthest — how can we check?
What could you change to make it go further?
Why do you think the heavy ball went further than the light one?

impact.text: Children investigate forces and motion, discovering steeper ramps make things go faster and further.
Children predict, test and adjust, changing one thing at a time to see the effect.
Children build and connect ramps and tubes, solving how to make a working run.
Children compare and measure distances — furthest, fastest, how far it rolled.
Children use the language of forces and motion — push, roll, fast, slow, steep.
Children persist with a run that won't work until it does, and feel the win.

enhancements: Ramps, guttering, cardboard tubes and blocks to build with.
A range of rollers — cars, balls, marbles, pom-poms — to compare.
Tape or chalk to mark and compare where things stop.
Blocks to raise and lower the ramps to different heights.
A target or gap to aim for, for real challenges.
A tuff-spot or floor track to keep the runs contained.
Timers or a finish line for the fastest-run races.

playing_exploring: Children experiment freely — steeper, heavier, longer — to see what happens.
They test every roller and every ramp height for themselves.
active_learning: Children keep rebuilding the run until it reaches the target.
They stay focused on making it go faster, further, higher.
creating_thinking: Children predict which will win and check by racing.
They change one thing at a time and work out why the result changed.
